free_tier.stated: free 90-day certificates including wildcards over DNS-01, with automated issuance and renewal

per_object_cap.stated: no certificate size cap; the binding limits are rate limits and not object caps

retention.stated: a certificate is valid 90 days and must be renewed; ARI lets a client renew early

interface_detail: the ACME v2 protocol at acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org, with a staging endpoint for testing
tooling: certbot, acme.sh, lego, Caddy, Traefik, any ACME client
chaining: free TLS on any name you control, including a wildcard, which is what makes the free-DNS plus free-tunnel chain terminate in a valid certificate

limits.value: 50 certificates per registered domain per 7 days, global across all accounts, refilling at 1 per 202 minutes
5 certificates per exact set of identifiers per 7 days
300 new orders per account per 3 hours
10 new accounts per IP per 3 hours
5 failed authorizations per identifier per account per hour; 1,152 consecutive failures then the identifier pauses
a certificate is valid 90 days; renewal is the client's job and there is no automatic extension

identity_cost.detail: no account is required to obtain a certificate; an ACME account key is generated locally and is not a registration
